propositions: Extraction from free-text LLM replies is currently heuristic: schema-valid decoys outside the intended payload can win, and fence-wrapping quoted JSON breaks fence-based channel markers.

An explicit output channel using line-anchored sentinel markers (<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> / <<<END>>>) makes payload location a stated contract rather than inference, with last-complete-block-wins semantics and fail-closed validation when markers are present.

The marker extraction must pair markers left-to-right non-nested (OPEN...OPEN...END yields one block; OPEN...END...OPEN...END yields two), treat marker lines as line-anchored (payload containing the literal marker string is safe), and fall back to full-reply selection when no complete block exists.

The bounded-retry prompt (structured_run.py retry tail) currently instructs bare JSON without markers, contradicting the first attempt's marker directive; it must be updated to name the same markers so the fail-closed retry channel is consistent.

The provider-parity test (test_provider_parity.py) assumes the directive is lead-in + one-line schema with nothing after; it must be re-derived to single-source and strip the entire directive (including the trailing sentinel wording) so both prompted arms remain identical.

Markerless and legacy replies must parse byte-for-byte identically to today (no regression), while marker-wrapped payloads must be extracted first (markers beat schema-selection decoys) and fail-closed if invalid, with no fallthrough to outside decoys.
